newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Second bombing raid in 12 hours on Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Second bombing raid in 12 hours on Kabul.

text.p: The anti-Taleban alliance launched two air raids on Kabul within 12 hours on Saturday night and Sunday morning.
There were no reports of casualties or major damage in the raids.
In the first raid, a single plane dropped at least four bombs at 1.15 a.m. (2045 GMT) in the vicinity of the airport.

"The air raid did not hit inside the airport perimeter. Two or three bombs landed close to the residential area north of here, but there are no reports of casualties," said Faizullah (eds: one name), the head of military security at the airport.
The night sky over Kabul was lit up as Taleban gunners fired tracer rounds and rocket propelled grenades at the departing aircraft, but there was no sign that it had been hit.
The second raid, at 12.20 p.m. (0750 GMT) on Sunday, was also aimed at the airport, and provoked a similar barrage of anti-aircraft and small arms fire.
The airport is used for both military and civilian traffic and has beed frequently targeted in the past.
Both the International Committee of the Red Cross and the United Nations use it for the transport of staff and supplies. Planes from both agencies landed between the raids.
The raids came on the same day as the opposition claimed to have pushed back the Taleban, capturing a strategic town and a nearby airbase from the Islamic warriors.

A senior opposition commander told Reuters on Sunday morning that their forces had captured the town of Charikar, 40 miles (64 km) north of Kabul, on Saturday night as well as the nearby Bagram airbase.
The commander, who preferred to remain anonymous, said their forces had killed 500 Taleban fighters in the battle.
There was no independent confirmation of the commander's claims, and Taleban fighters were preventing journalists from going to the front line.
